name: Retsin
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two touring bandmates from two different bands fell for each other on the road, made a record on an 8-track, and ended up trading electric guitars for banjo, flute and toy piano.

eras.title: Two vans cross paths
eras.text: Tara Jane O'Neil was bassist and singer in Louisville's Rodan; Cynthia Nelson played in Ruby Falls. They met in 1993 while both bands toured the country, and by 1994 they were a couple and a band, on the side of their day jobs.

years.h: Rodan's Tara Jane O'Neil meets Ruby Falls' Cynthia Nelson
years.p: Both were on national tours in 1993 when they met. AllMusic says they became a couple and started making music together in 1994.

years.cap: Both women had roles in the 1994 indie road movie Half-Cocked.
years.h: They both act in the indie road movie Half-Cocked
years.p: Filmed in Louisville, Nashville and Chattanooga, it follows a band that steals a van of gear; O'Neil and Nelson are in the cast alongside scene bands like Rodan, Unwound and Polvo.
years.xp:
Half-Cocked mixes actors with real indie bands playing themselves, and its cast list reads like a map of mid-90s underground rock. Wikipedia credits both O'Neil and Nelson as principal actors.

It is the film Retsin's Wikipedia entry ties to the duo's start, before their first record came out.

years.h: Rodan breaks up and O'Neil moves to New York
years.p: Wikipedia dates the end of [[Rodan|1e9250c4-46d2-48f1-b7c7-5f1c0a6b1abd]] to 1994, after which O'Neil relocated to New York and threw herself into Retsin and other projects.

eras.title: Salt Lick and Egg Fusion
eras.text: Retsin landed on Simple Machines, the DC-area label run by Tsunami's Jenny Toomey and Kristin Thomson, and put out two records in two years. Both were made by two people passing instruments back and forth, with friends filling in.

years.h: Salt Lick: eight songs, one 8-track, Simple Machines SMR 42
years.p: Part of it was recorded on a single 8-track in Louisville in September 1994, with more in New York and at WGNS Studios in DC in February 1995.
years.xp: The credits list Nelson and O'Neil on guitar, bass and vocals, with Steve Thornton on trombone, Jennifer Sharpe on steel guitar and Geoff Turner on guitar feedback and piano. Discogs lists it as an eight-track CD EP; Wikipedia calls it their debut album.

years.h: Egg Fusion: 14 songs recorded on Goddard Avenue in Louisville
years.p: Simple Machines SMR 46 was recorded in October 1995, and O'Neil played drums, keyboards and ocarina as well as guitar and bass.
years.xp: Per the liner notes, most tracks came from the house on Goddard Avenue, while a few, such as Duck Out, were 4-track recordings made in New York and Louisville. It was mixed at Falk Recording Studio.

years.h: On the road, with a rhythm section when they could get one
years.p: Wikipedia says they toured extensively behind the first record, sometimes adding a rhythm section for shows, and often just played as the duo.

eras.title: A label closes, a folk turn begins
eras.text: The duo left electric rock behind. Simple Machines shut down in 1998, and Retsin moved to Chicago's Carrot Top Records.

years.h: Sweet Luck of Amaryllis, first for Carrot Top
years.p: Todd Cook plays bass, with Tony Bailey and Greta Ritcher on drums for two songs; Temporary Residence also pressed it on vinyl as TRR 14.
years.xp: Reviewer Matt Dornan called it an album for lonely, rainy afternoons and singled out opener Lone Star Drive. AllMusic dates the group's shift from guitar rock toward folk instruments to the years after Simple Machines closed.

years.h: Simple Machines closes, and Retsin signs to Carrot Top
years.p: Wikipedia says the label's 1998 shutdown sent the band to Chicago's Carrot Top Records.

years.h: A duo that sounds like a whole band
years.p: AllMusic describes them by the end as a capable neo-folk outfit, largely done with standard rock instruments.

years.h: The Ida Retsin Family Volume One with the band Ida
years.p: A collaboration with the New York band Ida, released in 1998 on Muss My Hair Records.

eras.title: Cabin in the woods
eras.text: The last stretch was quiet and pastoral. Retsin made one more album, then both women joined Anna Padgett in a new band.

years.h: Cabin in the Woods: 15 songs of banjo, flute and toy piano
years.p: O'Neil plays guitar, banjo, toy piano and vocals; Nelson guitar, flute and vocals. Carrot Top released it in the US, with editions in France and Japan.
years.xp: Christian Quick mixed and mastered it, and O'Neil made the artwork. It is Retsin's last full-length.

years.cap: Cabin in the Woods, Carrot Top, 2001.
years.h: Moon Money Moon EP closes the discography
years.p: Acuarela Discos of Spain released the Moon Money Moon EP in 2001, the last Retsin release listed on Wikipedia.

years.h: O'Neil and Nelson join Anna Padgett in Naysayer
years.p: The side project recorded two albums, in 2001 and 2002, after which Retsin's story ends.

eras.title: After Retsin
eras.text: O'Neil launched a solo career in 2000 with Peregrine and has kept making records and visual art since.

years.h: Tara Jane O'Neil's solo debut, Peregrine
years.p: Her 2000 debut began a solo run that stretches to 2024's The Cool Cloud of Okayness, on labels including Quarterstick, K and Kranky.
